checks.title: Production hazardDeck() equals an independent re-implementation
checks.method: 4 modes × 3 containers × 8 client seeds × 150 nonces = 14,400 decks. Each deck compared element-wise with audit/lib/reference-rng.mjs, written from the specification only.

checks.title: Browser Web Crypto verifier accepts engine rounds for every stress client seed and mode
checks.assumption: public/fairness.js is the independent player-side check.
checks.method: For each mode × stress client seed × 6 nonces, play a deterministic round in the real engine (collect A at stop 1, B at stop 2, then sail until settled or collect at the final port), then run verifyRound() on publicRound().

checks.title: Rejection sampling is exactly unbiased for every bound used (2..20)
checks.method: For each bound b: limit = floor(2^32/b)·b; verify limit ≡ 0 (mod b), the rejected tail 2^32−limit < b, and every residue has exactly limit/b preimages. Then drive the reference shuffle with forced words: 0xFFFFFFFF first (must be rejected and consume an extra counter).
checks.note: Natural rejections occur with probability ≈ 1.607e-8 per deck, so they cannot be observed in practical samples; equivalence on natural data (R01) plus this forced-input test cover the path.

checks.title: Fisher–Yates form is a bijection between draw sequences and permutations
checks.assumption: Descending i from n−1 to 1, j uniform in [0, i] (as implemented).
checks.method: Generalise the implemented loop to n = 1..8 and enumerate every possible draw sequence (n! of them); require n! distinct permutations. Also confirm n = 20 has 20!/(h!(20−h)!) equally weighted h-prefix sets by counting multiplicities for n = 8, h = 3.

checks.title: HMAC message serialization is canonical and injective over stress inputs
checks.assumption: JSON.stringify of a fixed-shape array is unambiguous.
checks.method: Compare production randomMessage() with the reference serializer for all stress seeds; verify field order; verify 8 seeds × 3 containers × 3 nonces × 3 counters produce 216 distinct messages; confirm a separator-injection seed cannot collide with a genuine field split.
checks.note: Unpaired surrogates are escaped by JSON.stringify (ES2019 well-formed stringify), so Node createHmac and browser TextEncoder hash identical bytes.

checks.title: Seed commitment is SHA-256 over raw bytes; newSeed() emits 64 lowercase hex
checks.method: Compare seedHash() with reference over 1,000 derived seeds and confirm it differs from hashing the hex text. Draw 10,000 production newSeed() values (non-deterministic) and check format and uniqueness only.

checks.title: Difficulty is not part of the HMAC message: decks are nested across difficulties
checks.assumption: Observation about the documented algorithm, not a defect by itself.
checks.method: For 1,000 (seed, nonce, container) tuples compute decks for h = 1, 3, 5, 10 and test Easy ⊂ Medium ⊂ Hard ⊂ Expert.
checks.implication: Safe only because each committed server seed is consumed by exactly one round with one locked difficulty (verified in validate-system S05/S06). Any future feature that lets the same seed/nonce be replayed under a different difficulty would leak information across difficulties.

checks.title: Active-round responses never contain the server seed or hazard decks
checks.assumption: publicRound()/snapshot() are the only public projections.
checks.method: For 400 deterministic engine rounds, serialise publicRound() after every action while active and search for the raw seed, its hazards key and every hazard array; require revelation after settlement.
